records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The fallback calls recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential without a null check on the provider obtained from a string-id lookup that can return null (e.g. if the RECOVERY_CODES feature/provider is disabled in the deployment). When the recovery-codes feature is disabled but a custom userStorage returns false from updateCredential, users hit a NullPointerException (500) instead of a clean error; the provider was previously fetched via the typed factory constant in RecoveryAuthnCodesAction, where a missing provider was at least surfaced consistently.
records.rationale: In `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`, the provider is retrieved via `session.getProvider(CredentialProvider.class, "keycloak-recovery-authn-codes")` and stored in `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider` with no null check. If `user.credentialManager().updateCredential(...)` returns false, the code unconditionally calls `recoveryCodeCredentialProvider.createCredential(realm, user, credentialModel);`, which would throw a NullPointerException if the provider lookup returned null. This null-dereference path is directly present in the diff and is a correctness defect.

records.issue_text: [BUG] isValid() for recovery codes performs a plain equality match against the stored list but never removes or marks the consumed code as used, making recovery codes infinitely replayable in the federated path. In the local-storage path, Keycloak's RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialProvider invalidates a used code (the credential model's remaining-codes list is decremented on successful auth). The user-storage path added by this diff has no equivalent: the test demonstrates that a federated user can submit the same recovery code on every subsequent login forever, defeating the single-use guarantee that recovery codes exist to provide — an attacker who observes one code (e.g. shoulder-surf or a leaked page) gets permanent second-factor access. The product-side helper (CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential) provides no consumed-code update mechanism for user storage, so this gap is structural, not test-only.

records.issue_text: [BUG] createRecoveryCodesCredential wraps the IOException from JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString in a bare RuntimeException, aborting the required-action with an unhandled 500 after the user has already been shown the one-time recovery codes. If JSON serialization of the generated codes list fails, the user's browser shows the recovery codes page, clicks save, and gets a raw 500 (no INVALID_CREDENTIALS/controlled challenge, no error page per the required-action contract); the codes were displayed but never persisted, and the required action is silently left pending, so the user is stuck in a loop of generating codes that are never stored.
records.rationale: The diff adds `CredentialHelper.createRecoveryCodesCredential(...)`, which serializes `generatedCodes` via `JsonSerialization.writeValueAsString(generatedCodes)` and on failure does `catch (IOException e) { throw new RuntimeException(e); }`. This method is called directly from the required action `RecoveryAuthnCodesAction.processAction(...)` (`createRecoveryCodesCredential(reqActionContext.getSession(), ...)`). records.issue_text: [BUG] When the user storage accepts the credential (userStorageCreated == true), the hashed RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel is discarded and the plaintext generated codes are delivered via challengeResponse, so any user storage implementing updateCredential persists the raw codes with no hashed form anywhere. For user-storage users, the only persisted copy of recovery codes is the plaintext JSON in challengeResponse. When the credential is later consumed (a code used at login), Keycloak's consumption path updates via a RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel whose serialized credentialData is the hashed format, and the storage's later getCredentials/isValid deserializes it as List.class — readValue(List.class) on the hashed JSON object structure fails (IOException path) or the codes never match, so single-use consumption silently breaks for federated users after the first code use.
records.rationale: In the added user-storage implementation for recovery codes, validation is a pure membership check and never updates/removes the used code. Specifically, `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.isValid(...)` for `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.TYPE` deserializes the stored list and returns `generatedKeys.stream().anyMatch(key -> key.equals(input.getChallengeResponse()))`, with no subsequent `updateCredential(...)` or mutation of `myUser.recoveryCodes` to consume the code. records.issue_text: [BUG] The rewritten constructor still calls credentialModelOpt.get() on an Optional that getCredential can return empty, throwing NoSuchElementException instead of a controlled failure. A user whose recovery-codes credential is deleted (or whose user storage returns it via a path that isConfiguredFor accepts but getCredential filters out, e.g. a type-mismatched federated record) reaches the login form renderer and gets a raw 500 from template rendering rather than the configured invalid-credentials challenge.
records.rationale: In `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean`, the diff changes retrieval to `Optional<CredentialModel> credentialModelOpt = RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user);` but then still does `RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromCredentialModel(credentialModelOpt.get());` with no `isPresent()`/fallback. If `getCredential(user)` finds nothing in federated or stored credentials, this will throw `NoSuchElementException` during page rendering.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getCredentials silently drops the recovery-codes credential on deserialization failure, logging a message without the exception or username and still returning the OTP-only stream. If myUser.recoveryCodes.getCredentialData() is corrupt (e.g. after a consumption update stores the hashed JSON format that readValue(List.class) cannot parse), the user appears to have no recovery codes at all: isConfiguredFor still returns true (it checks the raw field) but the credential stream is empty, so getCredential() returns empty and the login bean throws NoSuchElementException — a silent partial-success state that the error log alone makes undiagnosable.
records.rationale: In `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials(...)`, recovery-codes deserialization failure is caught and only `log.error("Could not deserialize  credential of type: recovery-codes")` is emitted (no exception/username), then the method proceeds and returns a stream that may include only OTP (`credentialModels.add(myUser.getOtp())`).
